take:
In these 17 posts Codex most often appears next to Claude Code (9 posts tag both), and usually as the second opinion. @jens.heitmann installs the Codex CLI plus a GitHub skill so Claude Code can call Codex for tests and audits, arguing the two models catch different things ([audit setup](/e/DV3lILoEfzS)). Other creators formalize the split: a Codex plugin inside Claude Code where one model plans and reviews while GPT-5.6 executes, stretching two subscriptions' limits ([routing](/e/DaojVuSNKno)), and the Claudex skill, where Claude and GPT-6 Astra swap planner and auditor roles so neither grades its own work ([Claudex](/e/DeW79CbCkO3)). See the [earned-autonomy router guide](/guides/earned-autonomy-router).

On its own, Codex is shown running operations as much as code. One setup gives it three markdown context files (an about-me interview, a banned-phrases style list, a company file) and three daily checkpoints for triage, delegation and an end-of-day audit ([one-person company](/e/DdDT0X0KC64)). Another runs six scheduled Codex tasks a day for a stock-trading experiment, all posting into one thread; there are no results yet, and the entry itself calls one-month outperformance noise ([trading test](/e/Dc_qXENuDi4)). On the creative side, Codex drove Blender through a skills repo to build a 3D hero asset embedded with Three.js (2 posts tag Three.js), by a creator who had never used Blender ([Blender build](/e/DdUyTAAJTj6)).

Cost is the recurring argument for it: one tier list ranks Codex alongside Claude Code and says it gives comparable output for less money ([tier list](/e/DX7oRT3J1Hq)), and another creator builds dashboards on top of an existing Codex subscription instead of paying for API calls ([subscription UI](/e/DZErwKSCT2z)). ChatGPT co-occurs in 4 posts and Cursor in 2. Several tags are incidental: news roundups and repo lists that name Codex next to Claude Code ([Reverse Engineer Anything](/e/DeV2n53gLgf)), and one prompt-pack post with no content at all ([prompt pack](/e/Dc6Mq21TAyo)).
